summary: White County, TN tower on Milksick Mountain, run by the Tennessee Division of Forestry; only concrete footings remained by April 2018.

facts.status_note: Only concrete footings remained as of April 2018; no later description of the site found

events.note: Only concrete footings remained as of April 2018

evidence.supports: 50-foot metal cab Aermotor tower; only footings left by April 2018; standing into early 1990s
evidence.quote: As of April 2018, the only thing remaining of this 50-foot metal cab Aermotor tower was its concrete footings. The tower was still standing through at least the early 1990s.

According to local history and legend, Milksick Mountain gained its name after early settlers noticed that those who consumed the milk from cattle grazing on the mountain often became sick or even died.

evidence.supports: mountain fenced to keep cattle off
evidence.quote: Enough people were harmed that the mountain was eventually fenced off to keep the cattle from grazing there.

evidence.supports: administered by Tennessee Division of Forestry
evidence.quote: Administered by Tennessee Division of Forestry

evidence.supports: state list marks tower removed; elevation 1640 ft

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register gives 1,671 ft (509 m) for the site; the Tennessee tower list gives 1640 ft. Not resolved; the record keeps the register figure.

notes_for_editor: No build date, staffing or fire history in the sources read, so none is in the story. Access is unknown: no source after April 2018 describes the site. Elevation conflict between the register (1,671 ft) and the Tennessee list (1640 ft), unresolved. UCpedia's Milksick Mountain page returned HTTP 403 and was not used. Two web searches used; the second found no tower history.
